messages:
alina: quick pulse — profiler shows the hot path shifted when i switched the batch formation to the 'stochastic-slab' policy. kernel time on attention increased ~12% for medium-length prompts, but overall latency variance dropped. attaching quick notes.

ben: hmm, can you paste the flamegraph link or snippet? was this on nv-rtx or a dedicated p4d?

alina: ran on p4d-small (prod-like). flame: https://internal.tools/prof/3498765432/flame — main diff is kernel_select moving from 'fast-attn-v1' -> 'mixed-attn-tiling' for sequences ~120-260.

chloe: that v1->mixed switch matches our kernel selector heuristics: length distribution plus decode-rate estimate. maybe stochastic batching changed sequence coalescing so kernel chooser sees different avg seq length.

alina: exactly. i also saw KV cache churn up 8% for the same cohort; prefetch hit-rate dropped. suspect microbatch boundaries breaking long-request locality.

ben: ok, so two levers: batch formation and queue admission. i think we should tune token_budget upstream per workload bucket rather than global. right now token_budget=2000 static.

david: agreed. propose per-bucket policy: small/short, mid, long prompt buckets (by prompt tokens) and decode-rate buckets (slow/mid/fast). map (prompt_len, decode_rate) -> (max_microbatch, token_budget, admission_priority).

chloe: here's a straw config i've been testing:

```
workload_mapper_v2:
  buckets:
    - name: short_fast
      prompt_len: "<=32"
      decode_rate: ">120"
      max_microbatch: 8
      token_budget: 1024
      admission_priority: 80
    - name: mid_mid
      prompt_len: "33-128"
      decode_rate: "30-120"
      max_microbatch: 6
      token_budget: 2048
      admission_priority: 60
    - name: long_slow
      prompt_len: ">128"
      decode_rate: "<30"
      max_microbatch: 3
      token_budget: 4096
      admission_priority: 40
```

chloe: these are heuristic numbers; goal is to bias admission to keep KV reuse high for long sessions while letting short/fast collate more.

ben: interesting. how do we compute decode_rate at admission time? rolling estimate from client tokens/s or inference-side decode throughput?

alina: current classifier uses recent decode tokens/s observed on the request (last 500ms sampling). noisy but useful. we should smooth with EWMA and require N samples before bucket flip.

david: can we avoid flipping too often? hysteresis needed. add min-dwell 5s or require 2 consecutive samples. otherwise batching oscillates and we thrash kernels.

chloe: good call. also add a KV-prefetch threshold: if predicted next tokens > 256, prefetch KV shard to avoid eviction during microbatching. this reduced KV misses in my tests.

alina: i ran three A/B runs: baseline (static token_budget 2000) vs per-bucket (above) vs per-bucket + hysteresis + prefetch. results (p4d-small, mixed traffic):
- baseline: p95 latency 290ms, KV hit 0.86, avg kernel time 42ms
- buckets-only: p95 275ms, KV hit 0.81, avg kernel time 47ms (kernel slower due to mixed-attn in medium cohort)
- buckets+hysteresis+prefetch: p95 260ms, KV hit 0.89, avg kernel time 44ms

alina: so prefetch+hysteresis recovers KV and yields latency win despite some kernel slowdowns.

ben: nice. any regressions observed? alloc spikes, OOMs, or tail queuing?

alina: one regression: under bursty slow-decode traffic we saw increased queue depth and occasional microbatch creation overshoot leading to slightly higher p99 for long requests. likely due to admission_priority not penalizing long slow requests enough.

david: we can add per-cohort backpressure: if queue depth > threshold for cohort, reduce max_microbatch for that cohort for next N seconds. simple reactive control.

chloe: agree, implement backpressure policy and cap concurrent prefetched KV per device to avoid memory pressure. also reduce prefetch size from 256 -> 192 when GPU mem > 80%.

alina: plan: 1) land workload_mapper_v2 with buckets + hysteresis + prefetch (feature flag), 2) add cohort backpressure and prefetch cap, 3) run extended soak with mixed traffic and collect kernel selection traces and KV hit histogram.

ben: small ask: annotate kernel selector logs with cohort id and batch composition so we can see correlation in flamegraphs. can we add a lightweight tag in runtime?

alina: yes, will add `cohort_id` and `batch_signature` to the perf trace events. low overhead.

ops-bot: deploy plan created: canary rollout to 10% serving nodes at 15:00 UTC, auto-rollback if p95 increases > 8% or GPU mem > 85% for 5m.

david: cool. when do we start?

alina: scheduling canary today at 15:00 UTC. i'll ping eng-oncall and perf-monitoring. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
